## Explanation of the task 1

Task 1 examined whether adding uncertainty information made the underlying spatial
pattern in an EEG topoplot more difficult to recognize. On each trial, participants
saw a target ERP pattern and two alternative topoplots. They selected the alternative
that most closely matched the target. One alternative represented the same ERP-pattern
class as the target, while the other represented a different class.

The task included three characteristic ERP patterns: MMN, P3, and N170. Each was
shown using each of the seven visualization types. This produced 21 trials per
participant, each on separate page. Trial order was randomized separately for every
participant.

![Example comparison trial. Participants selected the alternative whose spatial pattern
most closely matched the target.](<../The Art of Uncertain Topoplots/figures/task1_explainer.png>){#fig-task1-explainer width=100% fig-alt="A target EEG topoplot above two alternative topoplots. A selection marker indicates that the participant chooses the alternative whose spatial pattern best matches the target."}

## Accuracy analysis

- Every response was coded as correct (`1`) or incorrect (`0`).

- The analysis contains `r format(task1_n_responses, big.mark = ",")` responses:
  `r task1_n_participants` participants × `r task1_n_trials` trials.

- Visualization type was treated as a categorical variable, with the basic topoplot as
  the reference condition.

- Presentation position was represented by the centered variable `position_c`,
  calculated as `position - mean(position)`. Because positions ranged from 1 to 21,
  their mean was 11. Thus, `position_c = 0` represents position 11, negative values
  represent earlier trials, and positive values represent later trials. This variable
  tests whether accuracy changed linearly as participants progressed through the task.

- No responses were excluded for missing values. All
  `r format(task1_n_responses, big.mark = ",")` reconstructed records
  contained accuracy, visualization type, ERP pattern, presentation position, target
  stimulus, and distractor stimulus.

```{r task1-stimulus-exposure}
task1_exposure <- task1_model |>
  mutate(across(c(stimulus, wrong_image), as.character)) |>
  group_by(ID) |>
  summarise(
    targets = n_distinct(stimulus),
    distractors = n_distinct(wrong_image),
    identities = n_distinct(c(stimulus, wrong_image)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
task1_n_identities <- n_distinct(c(
  as.character(task1_model$stimulus), as.character(task1_model$wrong_image)
))
task1_exposure_text <- function(x) {
  sprintf("%d--%d", min(x), max(x))
}
task1_n_saw_all <- sum(task1_exposure$identities == task1_n_identities)
```

- Stimulus assignment was incomplete but overlapping across participants. Across their
  `r task1_n_trials` trials, participants saw
  `r task1_exposure_text(task1_exposure$targets)` unique target stimuli
  (median `r median(task1_exposure$targets)`),
  `r task1_exposure_text(task1_exposure$distractors)` unique distractors
  (median `r median(task1_exposure$distractors)`), and
  `r task1_exposure_text(task1_exposure$identities)` unique stimulus identities
  across both roles (median `r median(task1_exposure$identities)`).
  `r if (task1_n_saw_all == 0) "No participant" else paste(task1_n_saw_all, if (task1_n_saw_all == 1) "participant" else "participants")`
  saw all `r task1_n_identities` stimulus identities. Because specific targets
  and distractors may differ in difficulty, this design motivates separate target- and
  distractor-stimulus random intercepts in the inferential model.

```{r}
task1_vistype_counts <- task1_model %>%
  count(vistype, name = "responses")

stopifnot(n_distinct(task1_vistype_counts$responses) == 1L)

task1_n_responses_per_vistype <- first(task1_vistype_counts$responses)
task1_n_patterns <- n_distinct(task1_model$pattern)
```

### Accuracy by visualisation type

- Accuracy was calculated as correct responses divided by all responses
  (`correct / (correct + incorrect)`). Each visualization type had
  `r format(task1_n_responses_per_vistype, big.mark = ",")` responses
  (`r task1_n_participants` participants × `r task1_n_patterns` trials). This is an
  unadjusted pooled proportion.

- For each visualization type, accuracy was first averaged across three trials
 within each participant and then summarized across participants.

- The dark-blue region shows the two-sided 95% *t*-confidence interval around the
  across-participant mean; opacity decreases beyond that interval.

```{r}
task1_gradient_participants <- task1_model |>
  group_by(ID, vistype) |>
  summarise(
    participant_accuracy = mean(correct),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

task1_gradient_order <- task1_gradient_participants |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(mean_accuracy = mean(participant_accuracy), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(mean_accuracy) |>
  pull(vistype) |>
  as.character()

task1_gradient_summary <- task1_gradient_participants |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(
    n_participants = n(),
    mean_accuracy = mean(participant_accuracy),
    se_accuracy = sd(participant_accuracy) / sqrt(n_participants),
    df = n_participants - 1,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = task1_gradient_order),
    y_position = as.numeric(vistype),
    lower_95 = mean_accuracy - qt(0.975, df) * se_accuracy,
    upper_95 = mean_accuracy + qt(0.975, df) * se_accuracy
  ) |>
  arrange(vistype)

task1_response_counts <- task1_model |>
  group_by(vistype) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_correct = sum(correct == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_incorrect = sum(correct == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    pooled_accuracy = mean(correct, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

vistype_table <- task1_response_counts |>
  left_join(
    task1_gradient_summary |>
      select(vistype, mean_accuracy, lower_95, upper_95),
    by = "vistype"
  )

stopifnot(
  all(task1_gradient_summary$n_participants == n_distinct(task1_model$ID)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    vistype_table$pooled_accuracy,
    vistype_table$mean_accuracy,
    tolerance = 1e-12
  ))
)

vistype_table |>
  mutate(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    mean_accuracy = scales::percent(mean_accuracy, accuracy = 0.1),
    lower_95 = scales::percent(lower_95, accuracy = 0.1),
    upper_95 = scales::percent(upper_95, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  select(-pooled_accuracy) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization type",
      "Responses",
      "Correct",
      "Incorrect",
      "Mean accuracy",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Observed comparison-task accuracy by visualization type",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

### Population-average accuracy

- A logistic mixed-effects model estimated the probability of a correct response:

  ```r
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)
  ```

- Some participants were generally more accurate than others. Because every participant
  completed 21 trials, we added a participant random intercept, which allows each
  participant to have their own baseline accuracy. The model then examines whether
  accuracy changed with visualization type or trial position across participants.

- ERP pattern was included as a fixed effect, so visualization comparisons account for
  systematic accuracy differences among MMN, N170, and P3 trials.

- Target and distractor stimuli were included as separate random intercepts. This gives
  each image its own baseline difficulty in each role and prevents unusually easy or
  difficult images from being mistaken for visualization effects.

- These probabilities are model-based estimates of average accuracy for each visualisation type.
Estimates were calculated for the midpoint of the experiment, weighted equally across the three ERP patterns, and averaged over participant and stimulus differences (random effects).

```{r}
#| include: false

# Logistic mixed-effects model
task1_fit <- glmer(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  data = task1_model,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

# Check whether the data support a participant-specific presentation-position slope.
task1_position_slope_fit <- glmer(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 + position_c | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  data = task1_model,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)
task1_position_slope_variance <- as.numeric(
  lme4::VarCorr(task1_position_slope_fit)$ID["position_c", "position_c"]
)
task1_position_slope_correlation <- as.numeric(
  attr(lme4::VarCorr(task1_position_slope_fit)$ID, "correlation")[
    "(Intercept)", "position_c"
  ]
)
task1_position_slope_singular <- lme4::isSingular(
  task1_position_slope_fit,
  tol = 1e-4
)

# Predictions are evaluated for every visualization-pattern combination and then
# averaged equally over the three experimentally controlled ERP patterns.
task1_vistype_levels <- levels(task1_model$vistype)
task1_pattern_levels <- levels(task1_model$pattern)
task1_prediction_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  vistype = factor(task1_vistype_levels, levels = task1_vistype_levels),
  pattern = factor(task1_pattern_levels, levels = task1_pattern_levels),
  position_c = 0
)

task1_average_over_patterns <- function(values) {
  vapply(
    task1_vistype_levels,
    function(visualization) {
      mean(values[as.character(task1_prediction_grid$vistype) == visualization])
    },
    numeric(1)
  )
}

task1_random_effect_sds <- function(model) {
  variance_components <- lme4::VarCorr(model)
  vapply(
    c("ID", "stimulus", "wrong_image"),
    function(group) as.numeric(attr(variance_components[[group]], "stddev")),
    numeric(1)
  )
}

# Population-average probabilities integrate over the fitted participant, target,
# and distractor random-intercept distributions. Their independent normal random
# intercepts sum to one normal distribution with the summed variance.
task1_population_probabilities <- function(model) {
  fixed_formula <- lme4::nobars(formula(model))
  fixed_terms <- delete.response(terms(fixed_formula))
  design_matrix <- model.matrix(fixed_terms, task1_prediction_grid)
  linear_predictor <- as.numeric(design_matrix %*% lme4::fixef(model))
  total_random_sd <- sqrt(sum(task1_random_effect_sds(model)^2))

  if (total_random_sd < sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)) {
    return(task1_average_over_patterns(plogis(linear_predictor)))
  }

  grid_probabilities <- vapply(
    linear_predictor,
    function(eta) {
      integrate(
        function(random_intercept) {
          plogis(eta + random_intercept) *
            dnorm(random_intercept, sd = total_random_sd)
        },
        lower = -Inf,
        upper = Inf,
        rel.tol = 1e-10
      )$value
    },
    numeric(1)
  )

  task1_average_over_patterns(grid_probabilities)
}

# Compare the three candidate summaries before selecting the reporting target.
task1_fixed_formula <- lme4::nobars(formula(task1_fit))
task1_fixed_terms <- delete.response(terms(task1_fixed_formula))
task1_design_matrix <- model.matrix(task1_fixed_terms, task1_prediction_grid)
task1_linear_predictor <- as.numeric(
  task1_design_matrix %*% lme4::fixef(task1_fit)
)
task1_participant_effects <- lme4::ranef(task1_fit)$ID[, 1]
task1_target_effects <- lme4::ranef(task1_fit)$stimulus[, 1]
task1_distractor_effects <- lme4::ranef(task1_fit)$wrong_image[, 1]
task1_fitted_random_effect_sums <- as.vector(
  outer(
    task1_participant_effects,
    as.vector(outer(task1_target_effects, task1_distractor_effects, "+")),
    "+"
  )
)

task1_conditional_probabilities <- task1_average_over_patterns(
  plogis(task1_linear_predictor)
)
task1_fitted_sample_probabilities <- task1_average_over_patterns(
  vapply(
    task1_linear_predictor,
    function(eta) mean(plogis(eta + task1_fitted_random_effect_sums)),
    numeric(1)
  )
)

task1_estimand_comparison <- tibble::tibble(
  vistype = factor(task1_vistype_levels, levels = task1_vistype_levels),
  conditional = task1_conditional_probabilities,
  fitted_sample = task1_fitted_sample_probabilities,
  population_average = task1_population_probabilities(task1_fit)
)

# Simulate fixed-effect uncertainty, then marginalize every draw over the fitted
# participant and stimulus distributions. This is much faster than model refitting.
set.seed(20261102)
task1_fixed_effect_draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(
  n = 10000,
  mu = lme4::fixef(task1_fit),
  Sigma = as.matrix(vcov(task1_fit))
)
task1_linear_predictor_draws <-
  task1_fixed_effect_draws %*% t(task1_design_matrix)
task1_random_effect_sd <- sqrt(sum(task1_random_effect_sds(task1_fit)^2))

# Twenty-point Gauss-Hermite quadrature accurately integrates the logistic-normal
# probabilities for all coefficient draws without model refitting.
task1_quadrature_order <- 20
task1_quadrature_matrix <- matrix(
  0,
  task1_quadrature_order,
  task1_quadrature_order
)
task1_quadrature_off_diagonal <- sqrt(
  seq_len(task1_quadrature_order - 1) / 2
)
task1_quadrature_matrix[
  cbind(
    seq_len(task1_quadrature_order - 1),
    2:task1_quadrature_order
  )
] <- task1_quadrature_off_diagonal
task1_quadrature_matrix[
  cbind(
    2:task1_quadrature_order,
    seq_len(task1_quadrature_order - 1)
  )
] <- task1_quadrature_off_diagonal
task1_quadrature <- eigen(task1_quadrature_matrix, symmetric = TRUE)
task1_quadrature_nodes <- task1_quadrature$values
task1_quadrature_weights <- task1_quadrature$vectors[1, ]^2

task1_population_draws_grid <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(task1_linear_predictor_draws),
  ncol = ncol(task1_linear_predictor_draws)
)
for (quadrature_index in seq_along(task1_quadrature_nodes)) {
  task1_population_draws_grid <- task1_population_draws_grid +
    task1_quadrature_weights[quadrature_index] *
    plogis(
      task1_linear_predictor_draws +
        sqrt(2) * task1_random_effect_sd *
        task1_quadrature_nodes[quadrature_index]
    )
}

task1_population_draws <- vapply(
  task1_vistype_levels,
  function(visualization) {
    rowMeans(
      task1_population_draws_grid[
        , as.character(task1_prediction_grid$vistype) == visualization,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    )
  },
  numeric(nrow(task1_population_draws_grid))
)

task1_probability_intervals <- apply(
  task1_population_draws,
  2,
  quantile,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

accuracy_estimates <- tibble::tibble(
  vistype = factor(task1_vistype_levels, levels = task1_vistype_levels),
  accuracy = task1_estimand_comparison$population_average,
  lower_ci = task1_probability_intervals[1, ],
  upper_ci = task1_probability_intervals[2, ]
) |>
  arrange(desc(accuracy)) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = rev(vistype))
  )

task1_conditional_gap <- max(abs(
  task1_estimand_comparison$population_average -
    task1_estimand_comparison$conditional
))
task1_sample_gap <- max(abs(
  task1_estimand_comparison$population_average -
    task1_estimand_comparison$fitted_sample
))
task1_conditional_gap_label <- sprintf(
  "%.1f percentage points",
  100 * task1_conditional_gap
)
task1_sample_gap_label <- sprintf(
  "%.1f percentage points",
  100 * task1_sample_gap
)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Choosing how to summarize predicted accuracy" collapse="true"}
There are three ways to summarize the model:

| Option | Calculation | What it describes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Set participant and stimulus differences to zero. | Average-baseline participants and stimuli. |
| 2 | Average over the participants and stimuli observed in the study, using their fitted random effects. | Sample-averaged model prediction. |
| 3 | Average over the modelled distributions of participant and stimulus random effects. | Population-averaged model prediction. |

We chose option 3 becausewe are more interested in accuracy over population
([Hu et al., 1998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9554609/);
[Hedeker et al., 2018](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5650580/)).

**Accuracy-averaging sensitivity check.** We compared Options 2 and 3. Across
visualisation types, the largest difference was `r task1_sample_gap_label`. This
difference did not meaningfully change the relative performance of the visualisation
types.

This does not make the sample representative of all EEG researchers.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why participant-specific random slopes were not retained

We tested whether the effect of trial position differed between participants by adding
a participant-specific position slope: `(1 + position_c | ID)`, while retaining the ERP
pattern and stimulus terms. The model
`r if (task1_position_slope_singular) "produced a singular fit and could not" else "did not produce a singular fit, but could only"`
estimate this additional variation:

- The estimated variance of the position slopes was
  `r sprintf("%.5f", task1_position_slope_variance)`.

- The estimated correlation between the baseline accuracy and position slopes was
  `r sprintf("%.2f", task1_position_slope_correlation)`.

`r if (task1_position_slope_singular) "Together, these boundary estimates indicate that the data did not contain enough information to estimate participant baseline differences and participant-specific position effects separately." else "Although the fit was not singular, the estimated slope variation was very small and did not justify the additional model complexity."`

We also considered participant-specific effects for visualization type. However, each
participant provided only three responses for each visualization. Modeling the
seven-level visualization factor would require six additional slopes and their
covariances, which the available responses could not support reliably.

We therefore retained the simpler random-intercept model. This does not show that the
position and visualization effects are identical for every participant. It means only
that these data cannot reliably estimate how those effects differ between participants.
:::

```{r}
accuracy_estimates |>
  mutate(
    vistype = table_vistype(vistype),
    across(
      c(accuracy, lower_ci, upper_ci),
      \(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 0.1)
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Visualization type",
      "Estimated accuracy",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Population-average comparison-task accuracy",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Binomial mixed-effects model with a logit link: ",
    "<code>correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c + (1 | ID) + ",
    "(1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",
    "<li><strong>ERP pattern:</strong> Predictions were averaged equally across MMN, ",
    "N170, and P3.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Trial position:</strong> Predicted accuracy was calculated at the ",
    "average presentation position.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Random effects:</strong> Predictions were averaged across the modeled ",
    "distributions of participant baseline accuracy and target- and distractor-stimulus ",
    "difficulty.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Confidence intervals:</strong> A separate 95% confidence interval ",
    "was calculated for each visualization type from 10,000 simulated sets of ",
    "fixed-effect estimates generated with <code>MASS::mvrnorm()</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Limitation:</strong> The estimated participant and stimulus ",
    "random-intercept variances were treated as fixed when calculating these ",
    "intervals.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model details"
)
```

### Accuracy differences relative to Basic topoplot

::: {.callout-note title="What is a contrast? — Expand" collapse="true"}
A **contrast** is one comparison computed from a model, for example "Confidence
intervals minus Basic topoplot".

| Type | What is compared | Adjustment | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Primary** (main results) | each uncertainty visualization vs Basic topoplot (6 per outcome) | Dunnett, for 6 comparisons | Task 1, Task 2, Hit or miss, Time, Subjective evaluation |
| **Secondary** | two uncertainty visualizations against each other (21 pairs) | Tukey, for 21 comparisons | Task 2, collapsed box |
| **Model coefficients** | every model term | none: for visualization rows, use the primary contrasts | coefficient tables |

A primary result counts as clear only if it holds after accounting for all six
comparisons.

**Definitions**

- **Adjustment (for multiple comparisons):** each extra comparison adds a chance of a
  false "difference". An adjustment widens intervals and raises *p* values so that the
  whole set of comparisons, not just one, stays at the 95% / 5% level.
- **Dunnett:** the adjustment for comparing several conditions with one reference
  (here, Basic topoplot).
- **Tukey:** the adjustment for comparing every condition with every other.
- **Unadjusted *p* value:** the *p* value of one comparison on its own, ignoring that
  others were made.
- **Model coefficient:** a number in the fitted model; for a visualization it is its
  difference from Basic topoplot on the model's scale (here, log odds).
:::

- These comparisons estimate the population-average accuracy difference between each
  visualization and the basic topoplot. They are the **primary comparisons** for Task 1.

- **Multiplicity.** The six comparisons with Basic form one family. Their intervals are
  simultaneous 95% confidence intervals with a Dunnett-type (max-|*z*|) adjustment: the
  critical value is the 95th percentile of the largest absolute standardized deviation
  across the six contrasts in the 10,000 simulated coefficient sets. The adjusted
  *p* values use the same distribution. An interval that crosses zero means that the
  visualization is not clearly different from Basic after this adjustment.

```{r task1-basic-contrast-figure}
#| cache: false
task1_basic_reference <- which(task1_vistype_levels == "basic")
task1_contrast_draws <- sweep(
  task1_population_draws,
  1,
  task1_population_draws[, task1_basic_reference],
  FUN = "-"
)
task1_contrast_estimates <-
  task1_estimand_comparison$population_average -
  task1_estimand_comparison$population_average[task1_basic_reference]

# Dunnett-type simultaneous inference for the six comparisons with Basic:
# standardize each simulated contrast, take the largest absolute value across the
# six contrasts in every draw, and use its 95th percentile as the critical value.
task1_contrast_columns <- setdiff(
  seq_along(task1_vistype_levels),
  task1_basic_reference
)
task1_contrast_sd <- apply(
  task1_contrast_draws[, task1_contrast_columns, drop = FALSE],
  2,
  sd
)
task1_contrast_z_draws <- sweep(
  sweep(
    task1_contrast_draws[, task1_contrast_columns, drop = FALSE],
    2,
    colMeans(task1_contrast_draws[, task1_contrast_columns, drop = FALSE])
  ),
  2,
  task1_contrast_sd,
  FUN = "/"
)
task1_max_abs_z <- apply(abs(task1_contrast_z_draws), 1, max)
task1_dunnett_critical <- unname(quantile(task1_max_abs_z, 0.95))
task1_contrast_z <-
  task1_contrast_estimates[task1_contrast_columns] / task1_contrast_sd

task1_basic_contrasts <- tibble::tibble(
  vistype = factor(
    task1_vistype_levels[task1_contrast_columns],
    levels = task1_vistype_levels
  ),
  difference = task1_contrast_estimates[task1_contrast_columns],
  standard_error = task1_contrast_sd,
  lower_ci = difference - task1_dunnett_critical * standard_error,
  upper_ci = difference + task1_dunnett_critical * standard_error,
  p_unadjusted = 2 * pnorm(abs(task1_contrast_z), lower.tail = FALSE),
  p_adjusted = vapply(
    abs(task1_contrast_z),
    \(z) mean(task1_max_abs_z >= z),
    numeric(1)
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = levels(accuracy_estimates$vistype))
  )

task1_contrast_limits <- c(
  max(-1, min(task1_basic_contrasts$lower_ci, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.03),
  min(1, max(task1_basic_contrasts$upper_ci, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.03)
)
```

### Model coefficients

- The coefficient table reports each visualization relative to the basic topoplot and
  reports the ERP-pattern and linear presentation-position effects. Coefficients are
  expressed as log odds. Its *p* values are **unadjusted** Wald tests of single
  coefficients.

- The second table gives the same six visualization comparisons as odds ratios with
  Dunnett-adjusted simultaneous intervals and *p* values (multivariate-*t* adjustment in
  `emmeans`, six comparisons with Basic). This is the odds-ratio counterpart of the
  primary contrasts above.

```{r}
model_order <- glmmTMB(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  family = binomial,
  data = task1_model
)

task1_model_coefficients <- summary(model_order)$coefficients$cond |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term")

task1_coefficient_results <- task1_model_coefficients |>
  transmute(
    term,
    term_label = dplyr::recode(
      .data$term,
      `(Intercept)` = "Basic topoplot (intercept)",
      vistypeadjacent = "Adjacent plots vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeanimation = "Animation vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_corner = "Bivariate corner vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypebivariate_range = "Bivariate range vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypetriple_CI = "Confidence intervals vs Basic topoplot",
      vistypeuncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers vs Basic topoplot",
      patternN170 = "N170 vs MMN pattern",
      patternP3 = "P3 vs MMN pattern",
      position_c = "Presentation position (centered)",
      .default = term
    ),
    estimate = Estimate,
    standard_error = .data[["Std. Error"]],
    z_value = .data[["z value"]],
    p_value = .data[["Pr(>|z|)"]],
    odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
    lower_or = exp(estimate - 1.96 * standard_error),
    upper_or = exp(estimate + 1.96 * standard_error)

task1_coefficient_results |>

model_table_note(

    "(1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)</code>.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Reference visualization:</strong> Basic topoplot.</li>",

task1_corner_result <- task1_coefficient_results |>
  filter(term == "vistypebivariate_corner")
task1_range_result <- task1_coefficient_results |>

task1_p3_result <- task1_coefficient_results |>
  filter(term == "patternP3")

  filter(term == "patternN170")
task1_position_result <- task1_coefficient_results |>
  filter(term == "position_c")

# Text helpers: every accuracy sentence on this page is generated from the
# estimates and their intervals. A difference is described as lower or higher
# only when its interval excludes the null value (1 for odds ratios, 0 for
# differences); otherwise the text says that the data cannot distinguish it from
# no difference.
task1_format_p <- function(p) {
  formatted <- format.pval(p, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)
  if_else(startsWith(formatted, "<"), formatted, paste("=", formatted))
}
task1_number_words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six")

task1_effect_sentence <- function(
  labels, estimate, lower, upper, p,
  scale = c("odds_ratio", "difference"),
  interval_text = "95% CI",
  p_text = "*p*",
  outcome = "the odds of a correct response were"
) {
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  null_value <- if (scale == "odds_ratio") 1 else 0
  describe <- function(i) {
    if (scale == "odds_ratio") {
      sprintf(
        "%s (OR = %.2f, %s %.2f–%.2f, %s %s)",
        labels[i], estimate[i], interval_text, lower[i], upper[i],
        p_text, task1_format_p(p[i])
      )
    } else {
      sprintf(
        "%s (%+.1f pp, %s %+.1f to %+.1f pp, %s %s)",
        labels[i], 100 * estimate[i], interval_text, 100 * lower[i],
        100 * upper[i], p_text, task1_format_p(p[i])
      )
    }
  }
  lower_set <- which(upper < null_value)
  higher_set <- which(lower > null_value)
  unclear_set <- setdiff(seq_along(estimate), c(lower_set, higher_set))
  sentences <- character()
  if (length(lower_set) > 0) {
    sentences <- c(sentences, paste0(
      "Relative to Basic topoplot, ", outcome, " clearly lower for ",
      knitr::combine_words(describe(lower_set)), "."
    ))
  }
  if (length(higher_set) > 0) {
    sentences <- c(sentences, paste0(
      "Relative to Basic topoplot, ", outcome, " clearly higher for ",
      knitr::combine_words(describe(higher_set)), "."
    ))
  }
  if (length(unclear_set) == length(estimate)) {
    sentences <- c(sentences, paste0(
      "No visualization type differed clearly from Basic topoplot: all ",
      task1_number_words[length(estimate)], " intervals included ",
      null_value, "."
    ))
  } else if (length(unclear_set) > 0) {
    sentences <- c(sentences, paste0(
      "The intervals for the other ", task1_number_words[length(unclear_set)],
      " visualization type", if (length(unclear_set) > 1) "s" else "",
      " included ", null_value, "."
    ))
  }
  # Name the unclear comparisons with the lowest point estimates, so that a
  # suggestive but inconclusive difference is reported with its uncertainty.
  below_null <- unclear_set[estimate[unclear_set] < null_value]
  below_null <- below_null[order(estimate[below_null])]
  below_null <- head(below_null, 2)
  if (length(below_null) > 0) {
    sentences <- c(sentences, paste0(
      "The lowest point estimate", if (length(below_null) > 1) "s were" else " was",
      " for ", knitr::combine_words(describe(below_null)),
      ", but ", if (length(below_null) > 1) "these intervals" else "this interval",
      " also included ", null_value,
      ", so the data are compatible both with no difference and with a ",
      if (scale == "odds_ratio") "moderate reduction in the odds." else
        "moderate accuracy cost."
    ))
  }
  paste(sentences, collapse = " ")
}

task1_visual_coefficients <- task1_coefficient_results |>
  filter(startsWith(term, "vistype"))

task1_coefficient_sentence <- task1_effect_sentence(
  labels = sub(" vs Basic topoplot$", "", task1_visual_coefficients$term_label),
  estimate = task1_visual_coefficients$odds_ratio,
  lower = task1_visual_coefficients$lower_or,
  upper = task1_visual_coefficients$upper_or,
  p = task1_visual_coefficients$p_value,
  interval_text = "unadjusted 95% CI",
  p_text = "unadjusted *p*"
)

task1_pattern_sentence <- function(result, label) {
  claim <- if (result$lower_or > 1) {
    "had higher odds of a correct response than MMN trials"
  } else if (result$upper_or < 1) {
    "had lower odds of a correct response than MMN trials"
  } else {
    "did not differ clearly from MMN trials"
  }
  sprintf(
    "%s trials %s (OR = %.2f, 95%% CI %.2f–%.2f, *p* %s)",
    label, claim,
    result$odds_ratio, result$lower_or, result$upper_or,
    task1_format_p(result$p_value)
  )
}
```

```{r task1-dunnett-odds-ratios}
set.seed(20261118)
```

#### Coefficient conclusion

**Unadjusted coefficients.** `r task1_coefficient_sentence`

**Dunnett-adjusted odds ratios.** `r task1_dunnett_or_sentence`

**Covariates.** `r task1_pattern_sentence(task1_p3_result, "P3")`;
`r task1_pattern_sentence(task1_n170_result, "N170")`. The overall
visualization-type test is reported below.

### Model fit comparison

- A likelihood-ratio test compares the model containing visualization type with a reduced
  model that retains ERP pattern, presentation position, and the same random effects. It
  evaluates whether visualization type improves the model overall after these adjustments.

```{r}
model_no_random_effects <- glmmTMB(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c,
  family = binomial,
  data = task1_model
)

model_no_vistype <- glmmTMB(
  correct ~ pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  family = binomial,
  data = task1_model
)

model_vistype <- glmmTMB(
  correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +
    (1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image),
  family = binomial,
  data = task1_model
)

task1_nested_comparison <- anova(model_no_vistype, model_vistype) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("model")

task1_vistype_lrt <- task1_nested_comparison[2, ]

task1_model_metrics <- function(fitted_model, label) {
  model_log_likelihood <- logLik(fitted_model)
  tibble::tibble(
    model = label,
    df = as.numeric(attr(model_log_likelihood, "df")),
    AIC = AIC(fitted_model),
    BIC = BIC(fitted_model),
    logLik = as.numeric(model_log_likelihood)
  )
}

task1_model_comparison_table <- bind_rows(
  task1_model_metrics(
    model_no_random_effects,
    paste0(
      "<code>correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c</code>"
    )
  ),
  task1_model_metrics(
    model_no_vistype,
    paste0(
      "<code>correct ~ pattern + position_c +<br>",
      "(1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)</code>"
    )
  ),
  task1_model_metrics(
    model_vistype,
    paste0(
      "<code>correct ~ vistype + pattern + position_c +<br>",
      "(1 | ID) + (1 | stimulus) + (1 | wrong_image)</code>"
    )
  )
)

format_best_model_fit <- function(values, direction = c("minimum", "maximum")) {
  direction <- match.arg(direction)
  best_value <- if (direction == "minimum") min(values) else max(values)
  formatted_values <- sprintf("%.3f", values)
  formatted_values[dplyr::near(values, best_value)] <- paste0(
    "<span class='best-model-fit'>",
    formatted_values[dplyr::near(values, best_value)],
    "</span>"
  )
  formatted_values
}

task1_model_comparison_display <- task1_model_comparison_table |>
  mutate(
    AIC = format_best_model_fit(AIC, "minimum"),
    BIC = format_best_model_fit(BIC, "minimum"),
    logLik = format_best_model_fit(logLik, "maximum")
  )

task1_model_comparison_display |>

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model family:</strong> Binomial models with a logit link.</li>",

    "improves fit while retaining the same random-effects structure.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Model comparison"
)
```

#### Model-comparison summary

Adding visualization type `r if (task1_vistype_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]] < 0.05) "improved" else "did not clearly improve"`
the adjusted model, $\chi^2(`r task1_vistype_lrt[["Chi Df"]]`) =
`r sprintf("%.2f", task1_vistype_lrt[["Chisq"]])`$,
*p* = `r format.pval(task1_vistype_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]], digits = 3, eps = 0.001)`.
The reduced and full models had AIC values of
`r sprintf("%.2f", task1_model_comparison_table$AIC[2])` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", task1_model_comparison_table$AIC[3])`, respectively, compared with
`r sprintf("%.2f", task1_model_comparison_table$AIC[1])` for the fixed-effects-only
model. Thus, after accounting for ERP
pattern, presentation position, participant baseline accuracy, and target- and
distractor-stimulus difficulty, the analysis
`r if (task1_vistype_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]] < 0.05) "provided evidence" else "did not provide clear evidence"`
that comparison-task accuracy differed overall among the seven visualization types.

## Conditional logistic paired-choice sensitivity analysis

Task 1 is a paired-choice experiment: every trial presents one matching and one
nonmatching candidate image. We therefore fitted a conditional logistic paired-choice
model as a sensitivity analysis. Its candidate-image terms provide a Bradley--Terry
representation of each image's general tendency to be selected. Unlike the primary
accuracy model, it assigns each of the 30 candidate images one shared attractiveness
parameter regardless of whether that image is matching or nonmatching on a particular
trial. It also adjusts for whether an image appeared as the second option.

The data were represented by two rows per trial, with one row for each candidate and
one selected candidate within each participant--trial choice set. Visualization effects
were estimated as interactions with matching-candidate status because visualization type
is constant within a choice set and its main effect therefore cancels. Standard errors
were clustered by participant to account for each participant's
`r task1_n_trials` choices.

```{r task1-bradley-terry-data}
task1_bt_trials <- task1 |>
  transmute(
    ID = factor(ID),
    trial,
    choice_set = interaction(ID, trial, drop = TRUE),
    vistype = relevel(factor(vistype), ref = "basic"),
    pattern = relevel(factor(pattern), ref = "MMN"),
    position_c = position - mean(position),
    stimulus = as.character(stimulus),
    correct_image = as.character(correct_image),
    wrong_image = as.character(wrong_image),
    solution,
    answered,
    recorded_correct = correct,
    opt1,
    opt2
  )

task1_bt_expected_opt1 <- if_else(
  task1_bt_trials$solution == 1L,
  task1_bt_trials$correct_image,
  task1_bt_trials$wrong_image
)
task1_bt_expected_opt2 <- if_else(
  task1_bt_trials$solution == 2L,
  task1_bt_trials$correct_image,
  task1_bt_trials$wrong_image
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(task1_bt_trials) == n_distinct(task1_bt_trials$choice_set),
  all(
    count(task1_bt_trials, ID, name = "trials")$trials == task1_n_trials
  ),
  all(task1_bt_trials$stimulus == task1_bt_trials$correct_image),
  all(task1_bt_trials$recorded_correct ==
        as.integer(task1_bt_trials$answered == task1_bt_trials$solution)),
  all(startsWith(
    basename(task1_bt_trials$opt1),
    paste0(task1_bt_expected_opt1, "_")
  )),
  all(startsWith(
    basename(task1_bt_trials$opt2),
    paste0(task1_bt_expected_opt2, "_")
  ))
)

task1_bt_choices <- bind_rows(
  task1_bt_trials |>
    transmute(
      ID,
      choice_set,
      vistype,
      pattern,
      position_c,
      option_second = 0L,
      candidate_image = if_else(
        solution == 1L,
        correct_image,
        wrong_image
      ),
      matches_target = as.integer(solution == 1L),
      chosen = as.integer(answered == 1L)
    ),
  task1_bt_trials |>
    transmute(
      ID,
      choice_set,
      vistype,
      pattern,
      position_c,
      option_second = 1L,
      candidate_image = if_else(
        solution == 2L,
        correct_image,
        wrong_image
      ),
      matches_target = as.integer(solution == 2L),
      chosen = as.integer(answered == 2L)
    )
) |>
  mutate(
    candidate_image = factor(candidate_image),
    match_adjacent = matches_target * as.integer(vistype == "adjacent"),
    match_animation = matches_target * as.integer(vistype == "animation"),
    match_bivariate_corner = matches_target *
      as.integer(vistype == "bivariate_corner"),
    match_bivariate_range = matches_target *
      as.integer(vistype == "bivariate_range"),
    match_triple_CI = matches_target * as.integer(vistype == "triple_CI"),
    match_uncert_markers = matches_target *
      as.integer(vistype == "uncert_markers"),
    match_N170 = matches_target * as.integer(pattern == "N170"),
    match_P3 = matches_target * as.integer(pattern == "P3"),
    match_position_c = matches_target * position_c
  )

task1_bt_choice_counts <- task1_bt_choices |>
  group_by(choice_set) |>
  summarise(
    alternatives = n(),
    selected = sum(chosen),
    matching = sum(matches_target),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(task1_bt_choices) == 2 * nrow(task1_bt_trials),
  all(task1_bt_choice_counts$alternatives == 2L),
  all(task1_bt_choice_counts$selected == 1L),
  all(task1_bt_choice_counts$matching == 1L),
  nlevels(task1_bt_choices$candidate_image) == 30L
)
```

```{r task1-bradley-terry-model}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))

task1_bt_fit <- clogit(
  chosen ~ matches_target +
    match_adjacent + match_animation +
    match_bivariate_corner + match_bivariate_range +
    match_triple_CI + match_uncert_markers +
    match_N170 + match_P3 + match_position_c +
    option_second + candidate_image +
    strata(choice_set) + cluster(ID),
  data = task1_bt_choices,
  method = "efron"
)
```

```{r task1-bradley-terry-results}
task1_bt_visual_terms <- c(
  "match_adjacent",
  "match_animation",
  "match_bivariate_corner",
  "match_bivariate_range",
  "match_triple_CI",
  "match_uncert_markers"
)
task1_bt_visual_labels <- c(
  "Adjacent plots vs Basic topoplot",
  "Animation vs Basic topoplot",
  "Bivariate corner vs Basic topoplot",
  "Bivariate range vs Basic topoplot",
  "Confidence intervals vs Basic topoplot",
  "Uncertainty markers vs Basic topoplot"
)

task1_bt_coefficients <- coef(task1_bt_fit)
task1_bt_covariance <- vcov(task1_bt_fit)
task1_bt_visual_estimates <- task1_bt_coefficients[task1_bt_visual_terms]
task1_bt_visual_standard_errors <- sqrt(
  diag(task1_bt_covariance)[task1_bt_visual_terms]
)

task1_bt_results <- tibble::tibble(
  comparison = task1_bt_visual_labels,
  estimate = unname(task1_bt_visual_estimates),
  standard_error = unname(task1_bt_visual_standard_errors)
) |>
  mutate(
    z_value = estimate / standard_error,
    p_value = 2 * pnorm(abs(z_value), lower.tail = FALSE),
    odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
    lower_ci = exp(estimate - 1.96 * standard_error),
    upper_ci = exp(estimate + 1.96 * standard_error)
  )

task1_bt_corner_result <- task1_bt_results |>
  filter(comparison == "Bivariate corner vs Basic topoplot")
task1_bt_range_result <- task1_bt_results |>
  filter(comparison == "Bivariate range vs Basic topoplot")

task1_bt_visual_covariance <- task1_bt_covariance[
  task1_bt_visual_terms,
  task1_bt_visual_terms,
  drop = FALSE
]
task1_bt_wald_chisq <- drop(
  t(task1_bt_visual_estimates) %*%
    solve(task1_bt_visual_covariance, task1_bt_visual_estimates)
)
task1_bt_wald_df <- length(task1_bt_visual_terms)
task1_bt_wald_p <- pchisq(
  task1_bt_wald_chisq,
  df = task1_bt_wald_df,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

# Dunnett-type adjustment for the six comparisons with Basic, from the joint
# normal distribution of the participant-clustered (robust) estimates.
task1_bt_correlation <- cov2cor(task1_bt_visual_covariance)
set.seed(20261118)
task1_bt_critical <- mvtnorm::qmvnorm(
  0.95,
  tail = "both.tails",
  corr = task1_bt_correlation
)$quantile
task1_bt_results <- task1_bt_results |>
  mutate(
    lower_adjusted = exp(estimate - task1_bt_critical * standard_error),
    upper_adjusted = exp(estimate + task1_bt_critical * standard_error),
    p_adjusted = vapply(
      abs(z_value),
      \(z) 1 - as.numeric(mvtnorm::pmvnorm(
        lower = rep(-z, length(task1_bt_visual_terms)),
        upper = rep(z, length(task1_bt_visual_terms)),
        corr = task1_bt_correlation
      )),
      numeric(1)
    )
  )

task1_bt_results |>
  transmute(
    Comparison = comparison,
    `Odds ratio` = sprintf("%.2f", odds_ratio),
    `95% CI (unadjusted)` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", lower_ci, upper_ci),
    `p (unadjusted)` = format.pval(p_value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    `Simultaneous 95% CI` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", lower_adjusted, upper_adjusted),
    `p (Dunnett-adjusted)` = format_pvalue_html(p_adjusted)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption = paste(
      "Conditional logistic paired-choice sensitivity analysis.",
      "Adjusted intervals and p values are Dunnett-type (multivariate normal)",
      "adjusted for the six comparisons with Basic, using participant-clustered",
      "standard errors. Adjusted values with p < .05 are shown in dark red."
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    "<li><strong>Model:</strong> Conditional logistic paired-choice model with one ",
    "stratum per participant--trial.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Bradley--Terry connection:</strong> Candidate-image effects represent ",
    "each image's shared tendency to be selected across pairings.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Image effects:</strong> One shared fixed attractiveness parameter was ",
    "estimated for each candidate image across matching and nonmatching roles.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Adjustment:</strong> Matching-candidate effects were adjusted for ERP ",
    "pattern, presentation position, and whether the candidate was shown second.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Repeated choices:</strong> Robust standard errors were clustered by ",
    "participant.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Interpretation:</strong> An odds ratio below 1 indicates weaker ",
    "preference for the matching candidate than under Basic topoplot.</li>",
    "<li><strong>Multiplicity:</strong> Both unadjusted and Dunnett-adjusted values ",
    "are shown; the joint robust Wald test is reported below.</li>",
    "</ul>"
  ),
  label = "Sensitivity-model details"
)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Terms explanation"}
- **Conditional:** The model compares the two candidate images within the same
  participant's trial. It uses the fact that exactly one candidate was selected and
  removes the separate baseline for each trial. The term does not refer to an
  experimental condition.
- **Stratum:** A stratum is one participant--trial choice set. It contains two rows:
  one for the matching candidate and one for the nonmatching candidate. The model
  compares candidates within this set, not candidates from different trials.
:::

#### Sensitivity-analysis conclusion

```{r task1-bt-text}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
task1_bt_labels <- sub(" vs Basic topoplot$", "", task1_bt_results$comparison)
task1_bt_unadjusted_sentence <- task1_effect_sentence(
  labels = task1_bt_labels,
  estimate = task1_bt_results$odds_ratio,
  lower = task1_bt_results$lower_ci,
  upper = task1_bt_results$upper_ci,
  p = task1_bt_results$p_value,
  interval_text = "unadjusted 95% CI",
  p_text = "unadjusted *p*",
  outcome = "the odds of selecting the matching candidate were"
)
task1_bt_adjusted_sentence <- task1_effect_sentence(
  labels = task1_bt_labels,
  estimate = task1_bt_results$odds_ratio,
  lower = task1_bt_results$lower_adjusted,
  upper = task1_bt_results$upper_adjusted,
  p = task1_bt_results$p_adjusted,
  interval_text = "simultaneous 95% CI",
  p_text = "adjusted *p*",
  outcome = "the odds of selecting the matching candidate were"
)
```

After accounting for candidate-image attractiveness, option position, ERP pattern, and
presentation position, the joint participant-clustered Wald test
`r if (task1_bt_wald_p < 0.05) "indicated" else "did not clearly indicate"` that
visualization type changed preference for the matching candidate,
$\chi^2(`r task1_bt_wald_df`) = `r sprintf("%.2f", task1_bt_wald_chisq)`$,
*p* `r task1_format_p(task1_bt_wald_p)`.

**Unadjusted.** `r task1_bt_unadjusted_sentence`

**Dunnett-adjusted.** `r task1_bt_adjusted_sentence`

The sensitivity analysis separates matching performance from images' general tendency
to be selected; it does not replace the primary mixed-effects accuracy analysis.

## Item-level diagnostic: target images below chance

```{r task1-item-diagnostic}
#| cache: false
# Answer-key checks: the matching candidate is the target stimulus, its file is the
# option named by the solution code, and "correct" equals answered == solution.
task1_key_checks <- task1 |>
  mutate(
    matching_file = if_else(solution == 1L, opt1, opt2),
    nonmatching_file = if_else(solution == 1L, opt2, opt1),
    key_ok = stimulus == correct_image &
      startsWith(basename(matching_file), paste0(correct_image, "_")) &
      startsWith(basename(nonmatching_file), paste0(wrong_image, "_")) &
      sub("_.*$", "", correct_image) == pattern &
      correct == as.integer(answered == solution)
  )
task1_key_failures <- sum(!task1_key_checks$key_ok)

task1_items <- task1 |>
  mutate(distractor_pattern = sub("_.*$", "", wrong_image))

task1_target_accuracy <- task1_items |>
  group_by(stimulus, pattern) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_correct = sum(correct),
    accuracy = mean(correct),
    accuracy_vs_n170 = mean(correct[distractor_pattern == "N170"]),
    n_vs_n170 = sum(distractor_pattern == "N170"),
    accuracy_vs_p3 = mean(correct[distractor_pattern == "P3"]),
    accuracy_vs_mmn = mean(correct[distractor_pattern == "MMN"]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    lower = map2_dbl(n_correct, n, \(x, n) binom.test(x, n)$conf.int[1]),
    upper = map2_dbl(n_correct, n, \(x, n) binom.test(x, n)$conf.int[2]),
    p_vs_chance = map2_dbl(n_correct, n, \(x, n) binom.test(x, n, 0.5)$p.value)
  ) |>
  arrange(accuracy)

task1_distractor_accuracy <- task1_items |>
  group_by(wrong_image) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

task1_below_chance <- task1_target_accuracy |>
  filter(accuracy < 0.5) |>
  left_join(
    task1_distractor_accuracy |>
      rename(stimulus = wrong_image, accuracy_as_distractor = accuracy,
             n_as_distractor = n),
    by = "stimulus"
  )

task1_pair_accuracy <- task1_items |>
  group_by(stimulus, wrong_image) |>
  summarise(n = n(), accuracy = mean(correct), .groups = "drop")
task1_worst_pair <- task1_pair_accuracy |>
  filter(n >= 10) |>
  slice_min(accuracy, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

task1_class_accuracy <- task1_items |>
  group_by(pattern, distractor_pattern) |>
  summarise(n = n(), accuracy = mean(correct), .groups = "drop")
task1_mmn_vs_n170 <- task1_class_accuracy |>
  filter(pattern == "MMN", distractor_pattern == "N170")
task1_mmn_vs_p3 <- task1_class_accuracy |>
  filter(pattern == "MMN", distractor_pattern == "P3")

task1_below_chance |>
  transmute(
    stimulus,
    n,
    accuracy = sprintf("%.1f%% [%.1f, %.1f]", 100 * accuracy, 100 * lower, 100 * upper),
    p_vs_chance = format.pval(p_vs_chance, digits = 2, eps = 0.001),
    vs_n170 = sprintf("%.1f%% (n = %d)", 100 * accuracy_vs_n170, n_vs_n170),
    vs_p3 = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * accuracy_vs_p3),
    as_distractor = sprintf("%.1f%% (n = %d)", 100 * accuracy_as_distractor,
                            n_as_distractor)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    col.names = c(
      "Target image",
      "Trials",
      "Accuracy [exact 95% CI]",
      "p vs 50% (binomial)",
      "Accuracy vs N170 distractor",
      "Accuracy vs P3 distractor",
      "Accuracy when this image is the distractor"
    ),
    caption = "Target images with accuracy below 50%, all visualization types pooled.",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

task1_class_accuracy |>
  transmute(
    pattern,
    distractor_pattern,
    n,
    accuracy = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * accuracy)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    align = c("l", "l", "r", "r"),
    col.names = c("Target class", "Distractor class", "Trials", "Accuracy"),
    caption = "Accuracy by target and distractor ERP class.",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

```{r task1-item-sensitivity}
#| include: false
# Sensitivity refit without the trials whose target is below chance. Documented
# here only; the primary analysis keeps every trial.
task1_model_without_hard <- task1_model |>
  filter(!stimulus %in% task1_below_chance$stimulus) |>
  droplevels()
task1_fit_without_hard <- update(task1_fit, data = task1_model_without_hard)
task1_fit_without_hard_null <- update(
  task1_fit_without_hard,
  . ~ . - vistype
)
task1_without_hard_lrt <- anova(
  task1_fit_without_hard_null,
  task1_fit_without_hard
)
task1_without_hard_p <- task1_without_hard_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2]
task1_without_hard_or <- emmeans::emmeans(task1_fit_without_hard, ~ vistype) |>
  emmeans::contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "basic", adjust = "mvt") |>
  summary(infer = TRUE, type = "response") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(label = table_vistype(sub(" / basic$", "", as.character(contrast))))
task1_without_hard_lowest <- task1_without_hard_or |>
  slice_min(odds.ratio, n = 2)
task1_without_hard_any <- any(
  task1_without_hard_or$asymp.UCL < 1 | task1_without_hard_or$asymp.LCL > 1
)
task1_hard_vistype_counts <- task1_model |>
  filter(stimulus %in% task1_below_chance$stimulus) |>
  count(vistype)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Diagnostic: are the below-chance targets mis-keyed?"}
**Question.** `r nrow(task1_below_chance)` target images were matched less often than
chance across all visualization types: `r knitr::combine_words(sprintf("%s (%.1f%%, n = %d)", task1_below_chance$stimulus, 100 * task1_below_chance$accuracy, task1_below_chance$n))`.
The lowest target–distractor combination with at least 10 trials was
`r task1_worst_pair$stimulus` against `r task1_worst_pair$wrong_image`
(`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * task1_worst_pair$accuracy)` correct,
n = `r task1_worst_pair$n`).

**Answer key.** The key is internally consistent: in
`r if (task1_key_failures == 0) "all" else paste("all but", task1_key_failures, "of the")`
`r format(nrow(task1_key_checks), big.mark = ",")` trials, the matching candidate is the
target image, its file name belongs to the target's ERP class and to the option named by
the solution code, the nonmatching file is the logged distractor, and the recorded
accuracy equals "answered = solution". There is no sign of a coding or key error.

**Ambiguity, not mis-keying.** The difficulty is specific to N170 distractors. When the
target was an MMN image, accuracy was
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * task1_mmn_vs_n170$accuracy)` against an N170 distractor and
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * task1_mmn_vs_p3$accuracy)` against a P3 distractor. For the
below-chance targets, accuracy against N170 distractors was
`r knitr::combine_words(sprintf("%.1f%% (%s)", 100 * task1_below_chance$accuracy_vs_n170, task1_below_chance$stimulus))`,
but against P3 distractors it was
`r knitr::combine_words(sprintf("%.1f%% (%s)", 100 * task1_below_chance$accuracy_vs_p3, task1_below_chance$stimulus))`.
As distractors, the same images were almost never chosen
(`r knitr::combine_words(sprintf("%.1f%% correct for %s", 100 * task1_below_chance$accuracy_as_distractor, task1_below_chance$stimulus))`).
Visual inspection of the stimuli (`Experimental stimuli/stimuli/SE/`) agrees: the MMN
and N170 class templates both show a frontal negativity with a posterior positivity.
These two MMN images are weak single-subject maps (colour scales of ±1.5 and ±1.7 µV) whose positivity is
lateral or temporal rather than posterior, whereas several N170 images (for example
N170_7, N170_12, and N170_16) closely resemble the MMN template. Participants therefore
picked the image that looked more like the template, which on these trials was the
distractor.

**Consequence for the analysis.** These trials are retained. Target and distractor
random intercepts absorb image difficulty, and the trials with these targets were spread
evenly over the visualization types (`r min(task1_hard_vistype_counts$n)`–`r max(task1_hard_vistype_counts$n)`
trials per type), so hard items add noise rather than bias.

*Exploratory refit.* Without the
`r format(nrow(task1_model) - nrow(task1_model_without_hard), big.mark = ",")` trials
whose target was one of these images, the likelihood-ratio test for visualization type
gave *p* `r task1_format_p(task1_without_hard_p)` (all trials:
*p* `r task1_format_p(task1_vistype_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]])`). The two lowest odds ratios
relative to Basic were
`r knitr::combine_words(sprintf("%s (OR = %.2f, Dunnett-adjusted simultaneous 95%% CI %.2f–%.2f, adjusted *p* %s)", task1_without_hard_lowest$label, task1_without_hard_lowest$odds.ratio, task1_without_hard_lowest$asymp.LCL, task1_without_hard_lowest$asymp.UCL, task1_format_p(task1_without_hard_lowest$p.value)))`;
`r if (task1_without_hard_any) "at least one adjusted interval excluded 1" else "all six adjusted intervals included 1"`.
The excluded images were chosen after looking at the data, so this refit is exploratory
and does not replace the primary analysis.

In the manuscript, the stimulus section should state that some single-subject MMN and
N170 topographies are similar, which makes MMN–N170 pairs harder.
:::

## Summary of the Task 1 accuracy evidence

```{r task1-summary-text}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
task1_primary_labels <- unname(
  table_vistype(as.character(task1_basic_contrasts$vistype))
)
task1_primary_sentence <- task1_effect_sentence(
  labels = task1_primary_labels,
  estimate = task1_basic_contrasts$difference,
  lower = task1_basic_contrasts$lower_ci,
  upper = task1_basic_contrasts$upper_ci,
  p = task1_basic_contrasts$p_adjusted,
  scale = "difference",
  interval_text = "simultaneous 95% CI",
  p_text = "adjusted *p*",
  outcome = "population-average accuracy was"
)
task1_any_primary_effect <- any(
  task1_basic_contrasts$upper_ci < 0 | task1_basic_contrasts$lower_ci > 0
)
task1_lrt_p <- task1_vistype_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]]

# Do the two visualizations with the lowest primary estimates also have the two
# lowest odds ratios in the conditional-logit sensitivity analysis?
task1_lowest_primary <- task1_basic_contrasts |>
  slice_min(difference, n = 2) |>
  pull(vistype) |>
  as.character()
task1_lowest_bt <- task1_bt_results |>
  mutate(vistype = c(
    "adjacent", "animation", "bivariate_corner", "bivariate_range",
    "triple_CI", "uncert_markers"
  )) |>
  slice_min(odds_ratio, n = 2) |>
  pull(vistype)
task1_lowest_consistent <- setequal(task1_lowest_primary, task1_lowest_bt)
task1_lowest_labels <- knitr::combine_words(table_vistype(task1_lowest_primary))

task1_interpretation <- if (task1_any_primary_effect) {
  paste0(
    "At least one primary contrast excludes zero after adjustment; see the ",
    "sentences above for which visualization types and in which direction."
  )
} else {
  paste0(
    "Taken together, the evidence that any uncertainty visualization changed ",
    "matching accuracy is weak: the overall test gave *p* ",
    task1_format_p(task1_lrt_p),
    ", and no Dunnett-adjusted contrast with Basic excluded zero. ",
    if (task1_lowest_consistent) {
      paste0(
        task1_lowest_labels, " had the lowest estimates in both the primary ",
        "model and the conditional-logit sensitivity analysis, so they are ",
        "candidates for a small accuracy cost, but this study cannot distinguish ",
        "that cost from no difference. "
      )
    } else {
      ""
    },
    "The results should be reported as estimates with intervals, not as ",
    "evidence that a visualization lowered accuracy."
  )
}
```

- **Overall test.** Adding visualization type
  `r if (task1_lrt_p < 0.05) "improved" else "did not clearly improve"` the primary
  model, $\chi^2(`r task1_vistype_lrt[["Chi Df"]]`) =
  `r sprintf("%.2f", task1_vistype_lrt[["Chisq"]])`$, *p* `r task1_format_p(task1_lrt_p)`.
- **Primary contrasts** (population-average accuracy, Dunnett-adjusted for six
  comparisons with Basic). `r task1_primary_sentence`
- **Odds-ratio scale** (Dunnett-adjusted). `r task1_dunnett_or_sentence`
- **Sensitivity analysis** (conditional logit, Dunnett-adjusted).
  `r task1_bt_adjusted_sentence`
- **Interpretation.** `r task1_interpretation`
